tests.prompt:
Create a complete Modal component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable dialog component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a dialog box shown above a dimmed page backdrop (scrim), blocking interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed or actioned. It has a title bar (with an optional close "x"), a body area for content, and usually a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.

Types (2):
- Default: A neutral dialog for standard confirmations and focused tasks - the primary action button uses this system's brand red, same as a standard Primary button.
  Primary action button: background:#FF031A; Hover: background:#d10215;
- Destructive: Used for irreversible or dangerous confirmations, like deleting data - the same dialog structure as Default, but the primary action button uses the fixed danger-red token and typically reads "Delete" instead of "Confirm".
  Primary action button: background:#ff031a; Hover: background:#d10215;

States (4, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - common for critical confirmations.

Size: Small - controls the dialog's max-width (320px). Other options: Small (320px) / Medium (440px) / Large (560px).

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill)

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Delete this file?"); Body text (text, e.g. "This action cannot be undone."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.

- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.

Build it as ONE reusable dialog component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a dialog box shown above a dimmed page backdrop (scrim), blocking interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed or actioned. It has a title bar (with an optional close "x"), a body area for content, and usually a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.

  Primary action button: background:#ff031a; Hover: background:#d10215;

States (4, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - common for critical confirmations.

Create a complete Modal component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable dialog component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a dialog box shown above a dimmed page backdrop (scrim), blocking interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed or actioned. It has a title bar (with an optional close "x"), a body area for content, and usually a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.

Types (2):
- Default: A neutral dialog for standard confirmations and focused tasks - the primary action button uses this system's brand red, same as a standard Primary button.
  Primary action button: background:#FF031A; Hover: background:#d10215;
- Destructive: Used for irreversible or dangerous confirmations, like deleting data - the same dialog structure as Default, but the primary action button uses the fixed danger-red token and typically reads "Delete" instead of "Confirm".
  Primary action button: background:#ff031a; Hover: background:#d10215;

States (4, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - common for critical confirmations.

Size: Medium - controls the dialog's max-width (440px). Other options: Small (320px) / Medium (440px) / Large (560px).

Corner radius: 4px - Compact - the user has explicitly chosen this, generate only this option.

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Delete this file?"); Body text (text, e.g. "This action cannot be undone."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).

Build it as ONE reusable dialog component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a dialog box shown above a dimmed page backdrop (scrim), blocking interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed or actioned. It has a title bar (with an optional close "x"), a body area for content, and usually a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.

Types (2):
- Default: A neutral dialog for standard confirmations and focused tasks - the primary action button uses this system's brand red, same as a standard Primary button.
  Primary action button: background:#FF031A; Hover: background:#d10215;
- Destructive: Used for irreversible or dangerous confirmations, like deleting data - the same dialog structure as Default, but the primary action button uses the fixed danger-red token and typically reads "Delete" instead of "Confirm".
  Primary action button: background:#ff031a; Hover: background:#d10215;

States (4, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - common for critical confirmations.

Build it as ONE reusable dialog component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a dialog box shown above a dimmed page backdrop (scrim), blocking interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed or actioned. States (4, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - common for critical confirmations.

title: Modal STABLE

default.prompt:
Create a complete Modal component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable dialog component controlled by properties (type, state, size, radius) - a dialog box shown above a dimmed page backdrop (scrim), blocking interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed or actioned. It has a title bar (with an optional close "x"), a body area for content, and usually a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.

Types (2):
- Default: A neutral dialog for standard confirmations and focused tasks - the primary action button uses this system's brand red, same as a standard Primary button.
  Primary action button: background:#FF031A; Hover: background:#d10215;
- Destructive: Used for irreversible or dangerous confirmations, like deleting data - the same dialog structure as Default, but the primary action button uses the fixed danger-red token and typically reads "Delete" instead of "Confirm".
  Primary action button: background:#ff031a; Hover: background:#d10215;

States (4, structural):
- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
- No close: title bar has NO close X, forcing the user to pick a footer action - common for critical confirmations.

Size: Medium - controls the dialog's max-width (440px). Other options: Small (320px) / Medium (440px) / Large (560px).

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill)

Component properties: Title (text, e.g. "Delete this file?"); Body text (text, e.g. "This action cannot be undone."); Show close button (boolean toggle, default on - when off, the header renders with no close X, the same visual result as the No-close state but driven as a property rather than a fixed state).
Show close button is currently: on.

OVERVIEW

Modal is a dialog box that appears above a dimmed backdrop to focus the user on one task or decision before returning them to the page - it blocks interaction with everything behind it until the user responds or explicitly closes it.

WHEN TO USE

A destructive-action confirmation - confirming a delete before it happens.
A short, focused task or form - terms acceptance, an onboarding step.
A media preview that needs full attention - viewing an image or document in detail.

WHEN NOT TO USE

A task that needs more room than a dialog comfortably allows - use Drawer, which slides in from an edge instead of interrupting the whole page.
A brief, non-blocking confirmation - use Toast or Alert - Modal's backdrop is a heavy interruption for something minor.
Frequent or repeated interruptions in a single flow - excessive modal use breaks flow; consider inline validation or a Drawer instead.

BEST PRACTICES

Give it a single clear purpose and a single primary action - avoid turning it into a small multi-purpose page.
Always provide an obvious way to close it (a visible close button and Escape), even when a primary action is required.
Keep destructive confirmations short and specific about the consequence, not a generic "Are you sure?"

DO AND DON'T

DO

Delete 3 files?

This cannot be undone.

Cancel
Delete

One decision, stated with its consequence, and a button that names the action rather than agreeing vaguely.

DON'T

Are you sure?

Please confirm.

No
Yes

"Are you sure?" with Yes/No never says what is about to happen, so the user confirms without knowing what they agreed to.

ACCESSIBILITY

Traps keyboard focus within the dialog while open, and restores it to the triggering element on close.
Exposed as role="dialog" with aria-modal="true" and an accessible name (its title via aria-labelledby), announced as soon as it opens - this is about focus management and interruption, not aria-live, since a Modal blocks and demands a response rather than passively announcing a status.
Escape always closes it, no matter the type or state. A visible close "x" is also available for Default and Destructive, unless explicitly hidden via the Show close property or the No-close state.

RELATED COMPONENTS

Drawer, Pop Confirm, Result.

- Default: title bar with close X, body, and a footer with Cancel/primary-action buttons.
- No footer: title bar with close X and body only - a purely informational dialog, no footer action buttons.
- Scrollable: body content has a fixed max-height with a fade-to-transparent gradient cueing more content below - footer still present.
